metadata.title: Infinigen API Reference
metadata.description: Low-level helper functions used by primitive scripts (e.g., outputs/chairs/variant_041/Chair_primitive.py). Each entry lists purpose, inputs, outputs/return, side-effects, and notes for replay fidelity.

replay_context: Many operations require OBJECT vs EDIT mode and correct selection/active object. Sanitized scripts explicitly open EDIT blocks with ViewportMode and issue the ops in-order.
All parameters are constants; scripts rename objects in creation order (obj_1..obj_N) and reference them by stable names.
Dematerialized outputs: primitive scripts do not assign materials; geometry/attributes/modifiers are sufficient to reproduce shape.
script_notes: All numeric parameters in primitive scripts are concrete constants (no symbolic values).
Object arguments are Blender bpy.types.Object references; in primitive code they appear as bpy.data.objects["obj_k"].
Unless specified, functions mutate objects in-place and return either the modified object or None.
imports: from infinigen.assets.utils.decorate import write_attribute, write_co, read_co, read_edge_center, read_edge_direction, remove_edges, remove_vertices, select_edges, solidify, subsurf
from infinigen.core.util import blender as butil

functions.name: bezier_curve
functions.signature: bezier_curve(anchors: tuple[np.ndarray | Sequence[float], np.ndarray | Sequence[float], np.ndarray | Sequence[float]], vector_locations: Sequence[int] = (), resolution: int | None = None, to_mesh: bool = True)
functions.purpose: Create a mesh from a 3D Bezier curve profile (seat outline, rails, etc.). Positional order matters: arg2 is vector_locations, arg3 is resolution.

inputs.name: anchors
inputs.description: Control points in object space (x, y, z).

inputs.name: vector_locations
inputs.description: Indices where the curve uses vector handles (sharp transitions); empty means automatic. This is the second positional argument.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Curve resolution (defaults to 12 if None). Must be an int; pass as the third positional argument or as a keyword, never as a list.

inputs.name: to_mesh
inputs.description: Whether to convert curve to mesh.

functions.returns: bpy.types.Object (MESH) created and linked to the active collection.
side_effects: Object name assigned afterward by script
functions.notes: Often followed by weld/mirror/solidify/subsurf and edit-mode grid fill.

functions.name: align_bezier
functions.signature: align_bezier(anchors: np.ndarray, axes: Sequence[Sequence[float] | None] | None = None, scale: Sequence[float] | np.ndarray | None = None, vector_locations: Sequence[int] = (), resolution: int | None = None, to_mesh: bool = True)
functions.purpose: Generate a curved limb/back element by aligning a Bezier edge path between start/end points, with optional axis/scale profiles. Positional order matters: arg4 is vector_locations, arg5 is resolution.

inputs.name: anchors
inputs.description: Shape (3, N) or equivalent describing positions along the limb.

inputs.name: axes
inputs.type: list/array of direction vectors or None
inputs.description: Direction vectors or None to infer.

inputs.name: scale
inputs.description: Profile scales along the path, or None.

inputs.name: vector_locations
inputs.description: Indices where vector handles are used. This is the fourth positional argument.

inputs.name: resolution
inputs.description: Curve resolution. Must be an int; this is the fifth positional argument or may be passed by keyword.

side_effects: Scripts often set obj.location then apply transform
functions.notes: Common for legs/backs/arms; typically followed by weld and radius/solidify.
functions.implementation:
def align_bezier(
    anchors, axes=None, scale=None, vector_locations=(), resolution=None, to_mesh=True
):
    obj = bezier_curve(anchors, vector_locations, resolution, False)
    points = obj.data.splines[0].bezier_points
    if scale is None:
        scale = np.ones(2 * len(points) - 2)
    if axes is None:
        axes = [None] * len(points)
    scale = [1, *scale, 1]
    for i, p in enumerate(points):
        a = axes[i]
        if a is None:
            continue
        a = np.array(a)
        p.handle_left_type = "FREE"
        p.handle_right_type = "FREE"
        proj_left = np.array(p.handle_left - p.co) @ a * a
        p.handle_left = (
            np.array(p.co)
            + proj_left
            / np.linalg.norm(proj_left)
            * np.linalg.norm(p.handle_left - p.co)
            * scale[2 * i]
        )
        proj_right = np.array(p.handle_right - p.co) @ a * a
        p.handle_right = (
            np.array(p.co)
            + proj_right
            / np.linalg.norm(proj_right)
            * np.linalg.norm(p.handle_right - p.co)
            * scale[2 * i + 1]
        )
    if not to_mesh:
        return obj
    return curve2mesh(obj)

functions.name: write_attribute
functions.signature: write_attribute(obj: bpy.types.Object, value: int | float, name: str, domain: str = "POINT", data_type: str = "FLOAT")
functions.purpose: Write/ensure a mesh attribute with a constant value across a given domain (e.g., mark faces as "limb" or "panel").
side_effects: Ensures attribute exists on obj.data.attributes and sets values
functions.notes: Sanitized scripts may omit semantic attributes if not required for geometry reproduction.

functions.name: write_co
functions.signature: write_co(obj: bpy.types.Object, arr: np.ndarray)
functions.purpose: Overwrite vertex coordinates with the provided array.

inputs.name: arr
inputs.description: Array of shape (V, 3) where V must exactly match the current vertex count of obj (len(obj.data.vertices)). A mismatch causes RuntimeError.

functions.notes: IMPORTANT: arr.shape[0] must exactly equal len(obj.data.vertices). Raises RuntimeError on mismatch. Operations that change vertex count (join_objects, modifiers like SUBSURF/BEVEL/SOLIDIFY, bridge_edge_loops, fill_grid) invalidate any previously captured coordinate array. Always call write_co immediately after the object reaches its target vertex topology, before applying any vertex-count-changing modifiers.

functions.name: read_co
functions.signature: read_co(obj: bpy.types.Object) -> np.ndarray
functions.purpose: Read all vertex positions of a mesh into a (V, 3) numpy array. Used to query live geometry before computing predicate-based selections, anchor lookups, or in-place coordinate edits.

inputs.name: obj
inputs.description: MESH object whose vertex coordinates will be read.

functions.returns: np.ndarray of shape (V, 3) with float vertex coordinates in object space, where V == len(obj.data.vertices).
functions.notes: Pairs naturally with write_co for read-modify-write patterns: arr = read_co(obj); arr[...] = ...; write_co(obj, arr). Also commonly indexed via numpy ops like np.argmin(np.abs(arr[:, -1] - z)) to find a specific anchor vertex by coordinate. The returned array is a fresh copy, not a view; subsequent topology-changing operations (modifiers, joins, fill_grid, bridge_edge_loops) invalidate any assumption that the indices still correspond to the same vertices.

functions.name: read_edge_center
functions.signature: read_edge_center(obj: bpy.types.Object) -> np.ndarray
functions.purpose: Compute the midpoint of every edge in a mesh as a (E, 3) numpy array. Used to build per-edge boolean predicates (e.g., select edges whose center z lies within a band) without enumerating indices.

inputs.name: obj
inputs.description: MESH object whose edge centers will be computed.

functions.returns: np.ndarray of shape (E, 3) where E == len(obj.data.edges); each row is (v0 + v1) / 2 for that edge.
functions.notes: Typical pattern: c = read_edge_center(obj); select_edges(obj, (zmin <= c[:, -1]) & (c[:, -1] <= zmax)). The returned array reflects the current topology at call time; if a subsequent op (e.g., bridge_edge_loops) changes the edge set, you must re-read before issuing more predicate-based selections.

functions.name: read_edge_direction
functions.signature: read_edge_direction(obj: bpy.types.Object) -> np.ndarray
functions.purpose: Compute a unit-length direction vector for every edge in a mesh as a (E, 3) numpy array. Used to build orientation-based predicates (e.g., remove edges that are not vertical).

inputs.name: obj
inputs.description: MESH object whose per-edge directions will be computed.

functions.returns: np.ndarray of shape (E, 3); each row is the unit vector (v1 - v0) / ||v1 - v0|| for that edge.
functions.notes: Direction sign depends on the stored vertex order of each edge; predicates should typically use np.abs on a chosen component to be sign-agnostic, e.g., remove_edges(obj, np.abs(read_edge_direction(obj)[:, -1]) < 0.5).

functions.name: remove_edges
functions.signature: remove_edges(obj: bpy.types.Object, idxs: Iterable[int] | np.ndarray | Callable)
functions.purpose: Remove edges identified by indices, a boolean mask over edges, or a position-based predicate callable.

inputs.name: idxs
inputs.type: iterable of edge indices, boolean ndarray of length E, or callable
inputs.description: If iterable/ndarray: passed to np.nonzero (so a boolean mask of length E selects all True entries; an int iterable selects those edges directly). If callable: invoked as fn(x, y, z) where x, y, z are the per-edge centers from read_edge_center(obj), and must return a boolean mask.

side_effects: May remove faces as a consequence
functions.notes: v2 sanitized scripts pass a boolean ndarray built from read_edge_direction(obj) or read_edge_center(obj), e.g., remove_edges(obj, np.abs(read_edge_direction(obj)[:, -1]) < 0.5).
functions.implementation:
def remove_edges(obj, to_delete):
    if not isinstance(to_delete, Iterable):
        x, y, z = read_edge_center(obj).T
        to_delete = to_delete(x, y, z)
    to_delete = np.nonzero(to_delete)[0]
    with butil.ViewportMode(obj, "EDIT"):
        bm = bmesh.from_edit_mesh(obj.data)
        bm.edges.ensure_lookup_table()
        geom = [bm.edges[_] for _ in to_delete]
        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=geom, context="EDGES_FACES")
        bmesh.update_edit_mesh(obj.data)
    return obj

functions.name: remove_vertices
functions.signature: remove_vertices(obj: bpy.types.Object, idxs: Iterable[int] | np.ndarray | Callable)
functions.purpose: Remove vertices (and associated elements) identified by indices, a boolean mask over vertices, or a position-based predicate callable.

inputs.name: idxs
inputs.type: iterable of vertex indices, boolean ndarray of length V, or callable
inputs.description: If iterable/ndarray: passed to np.nonzero (so a boolean mask of length V selects all True entries; an int iterable selects those vertices directly). If callable: invoked as fn(x, y, z) where x, y, z are per-vertex coordinates from read_co(obj), and must return a boolean mask.

functions.notes: v2 sanitized scripts may pass either a callable lambda (e.g., lambda x, y, z: z < -thickness/2) or a precomputed boolean mask derived from read_co(obj).
functions.implementation:
def remove_vertices(obj, to_delete):
    if not isinstance(to_delete, Iterable):
        x, y, z = read_co(obj).T
        to_delete = to_delete(x, y, z)
    to_delete = np.nonzero(to_delete)[0]
    with butil.ViewportMode(obj, "EDIT"):
        bm = bmesh.from_edit_mesh(obj.data)
        bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
        geom = [bm.verts[_] for _ in to_delete]
        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=geom)
        bmesh.update_edit_mesh(obj.data)
    return obj

functions.name: select_edges
functions.signature: select_edges(obj: bpy.types.Object, idxs: Iterable[int] | np.ndarray | Callable)
functions.purpose: Select edges in EDIT mode by indices, a boolean mask over edges, or a position-based predicate callable.

inputs.name: idxs
inputs.type: iterable of edge indices, boolean ndarray of length E, or callable
inputs.description: If iterable/ndarray: passed to np.nonzero (so a boolean mask of length E selects all True entries; an int iterable selects those edges directly). If callable: invoked as fn(x, y, z) where x, y, z are per-edge centers from read_edge_center(obj), and must return a boolean mask.

side_effects: Switches obj into EDIT mode for the duration of the call (and back to OBJECT)
Replaces the current edge selection (deselects all first)
functions.notes: v2 sanitized scripts cache c = read_edge_center(obj) once and then issue per-band predicates such as select_edges(obj, (zmin <= c[:, -1]) & (c[:, -1] <= zmax)). Each call deselects everything before reselecting, so a follow-up bridge_edge_loops/extrude only acts on the freshly selected band. Re-read read_edge_center after any topology-changing op (e.g., bridge_edge_loops) before issuing more predicate selections.
functions.implementation:
def select_edges(obj, to_select):
    if not isinstance(to_select, Iterable):
        x, y, z = read_edge_center(obj).T
        to_select = to_select(x, y, z)
    to_select = np.nonzero(to_select)[0]
    with butil.ViewportMode(obj, "EDIT"):
        bpy.ops.mesh.select_mode(type="EDGE")
        bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action="DESELECT")
        bm = bmesh.from_edit_mesh(obj.data)
        bm.edges.ensure_lookup_table()
        for i in to_select:
            bm.edges[i].select_set(True)
        bm.select_flush(False)
        bmesh.update_edit_mesh(obj.data)
    return obj

functions.name: subsurf
functions.signature: subsurf(obj: bpy.types.Object, levels: int, simple: bool = False)
functions.purpose: Add/adjust a Subdivision Surface modifier.

inputs.name: simple
inputs.description: Use Simple subdivision instead of Catmull-Clark.

side_effects: May or may not apply immediately
functions.notes: Only adds modifier if levels > 0.

functions.name: solidify
functions.signature: solidify(obj: bpy.types.Object, axis: int, thickness: float)
functions.purpose: Give thickness or radius to limbs/panels.

inputs.name: axis
inputs.description: Axis along which to extrude (0, 1, or 2).

side_effects: Depending on limb style, either uses a custom nodegroup (radius) or adds SOLIDIFY and BEVEL
Modifies object location and applies transform
functions.notes: Extrudes along two perpendicular axes to create thickness.
functions.implementation:
def solidify(obj, axis, thickness):
    axes = [0, 1, 2]
    axes.remove(axis)
    u = np.zeros(3)
    u[axes[0]] = thickness
    v = np.zeros(3)
    v[axes[1]] = thickness
    butil.select_none()
    with butil.ViewportMode(obj, "EDIT"):
        bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action="SELECT")
        bpy.ops.mesh.extrude_edges_move(TRANSFORM_OT_translate={"value": u})
        bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action="SELECT")
        bpy.ops.mesh.extrude_region_move(TRANSFORM_OT_translate={"value": v})
    obj.location = -(u + v) / 2
    butil.apply_transform(obj, True)
    return obj

functions.name: join_objects
functions.signature: join_objects(objs: bpy.types.Object | Sequence[bpy.types.Object])
functions.purpose: Join multiple mesh objects into the first active object.

inputs.name: objs
inputs.type: list of bpy.types.Object (MESH) or single object
inputs.description: Objects to join. Can be a list or single object.

side_effects: Removes other objects by merging data
Resets location, rotation, and scale of merged object
functions.notes: Sanitized scripts generally avoid global final join; may join specific temporary parts during back decor creation.
functions.implementation:
def join_objects(obj):
    butil.select_none()
    if not isinstance(obj, list):
        obj = [obj]
    if len(obj) == 1:
        return obj[0]
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj[0]
    butil.select_none()
    butil.select(obj)
    bpy.ops.object.join()
    obj = bpy.context.active_object
    obj.location = 0, 0, 0
    obj.rotation_euler = 0, 0, 0
    obj.scale = 1, 1, 1
    butil.select_none()
    return obj

functions.name: new_bbox
functions.signature: new_bbox(xmin: float, xmax: float, ymin: float, ymax: float, zmin: float, zmax: float)
functions.purpose: Create a bounding-box mesh primitive.
functions.returns: bpy.types.Object (MESH) for the box, linked to the scene.
side_effects: Creates and links new object to scene
functions.notes: Creates a cube and scales/positions it to match the bounding box extents.
functions.implementation:
def new_bbox(x, x_, y, y_, z, z_):
    obj = new_cube()
    obj.location = (x + x_) / 2, (y + y_) / 2, (z + z_) / 2
    obj.scale = (x_ - x) / 2, (y_ - y) / 2, (z_ - z) / 2
    butil.apply_transform(obj, True)
    return obj

functions.name: geo_radius
functions.signature: geo_radius(nw: NodeWrangler, radius: float | Callable, resolution: int = 6, merge_distance: float = 0.004, rotation: float = 0, to_align_tilt: bool = True, align_tilt_axis: tuple[float, float, float] = (0, 0, 1))
functions.purpose: Nodegroup function/reference used to add a thickness/radius via Geometry Nodes.

inputs.name: nw
inputs.description: NodeWrangler instance for building geometry nodes.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: Radius value or function to evaluate.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Rotation angle for the profile circle.

side_effects: Creates geometry nodes modifier when used with surface.add_geomod
functions.notes: In primitive scripts, only geo_radius is referenced (other closures are not serializable and are skipped). Usage: Passed to surface.add_geomod(obj, geo_radius, ...).

functions.name: modify_mesh
functions.signature: butil.modify_mesh(obj: bpy.types.Object, type: str, apply: bool = True, name: str | None = None, return_mod: bool = False, ng_inputs: dict | None = None, show_viewport: bool | None = None, **kwargs)
functions.purpose: Create/configure/apply a standard Blender modifier on an object (e.g., WELD, MIRROR, SOLIDIFY, SUBSURF, BEVEL).

inputs.name: apply
inputs.description: Whether to apply the modifier immediately.

inputs.name: return_mod
inputs.description: Whether to return the modifier object.

inputs.name: show_viewport
inputs.description: Whether to show modifier in viewport.

inputs.name: **kwargs
inputs.description: Modifier properties (e.g., merge_threshold, levels, width, segments, offset).

functions.returns: obj (or obj, mod if return_mod=True and not applied).
side_effects: Creates and optionally applies a Blender modifier in correct order
functions.notes: Standard way to add modifiers in primitive scripts.

functions.name: apply_transform
functions.signature: butil.apply_transform(obj: bpy.types.Object, loc: bool = False, rot: bool = True, scale: bool = True)
functions.purpose: Apply object transforms (location, rotation, scale) to bake geometry.
functions.notes: Sanitized usage: Typically rot=True, scale=True (and sometimes loc=True), emitted explicitly.

functions.name: apply_modifiers
functions.signature: butil.apply_modifiers(obj: bpy.types.Object, mod: str | object | list | None = None, quiet: bool = True)
functions.purpose: Apply one or multiple modifiers.

inputs.name: mod
inputs.description: Specific modifier(s) to apply, or None for all.

functions.notes: Used to bake modifier effects into geometry.

functions.name: deep_clone_obj
functions.signature: deep_clone_obj(obj: bpy.types.Object, keep_modifiers: bool = False, keep_materials: bool = False)
functions.purpose: Duplicate object and its mesh data, linking clone to scene.

inputs.name: keep_modifiers
inputs.description: Whether to keep modifiers on clone.

inputs.name: keep_materials
inputs.description: Whether to keep materials on clone.

functions.notes: Creates independent copy of object and mesh data.

functions.name: add_geomod
functions.signature: surface.add_geomod(objs: bpy.types.Object | Sequence[bpy.types.Object], geo_func: Callable, name: str | None = None, apply: bool = False, reuse: bool = False, input_args: list | None = None, input_kwargs: dict | None = None, attributes: list | None = None, show_viewport: bool = True, selection: np.ndarray | None = None, domains: list | None = None, input_attributes: list | None = None)
functions.purpose: Add a Geometry Nodes modifier based on a nodegroup (e.g., geo_radius) and optionally apply.

inputs.name: apply
inputs.description: Whether to apply the modifier immediately.

inputs.name: reuse
inputs.description: Whether to reuse existing node group.

inputs.name: show_viewport
inputs.description: Whether to show modifier in viewport.

functions.notes: Sanitized scripts only use resolvable nodegroups like geo_radius.

examples.description: Create a seat surface from anchors and fill
examples.code:
obj = bezier_curve((np.array([...]), np.array([...]), np.array([...])), vector_locations=[4], resolution=12)
butil.modify_mesh(obj, 'WELD', merge_threshold=0.001)
with butil.ViewportMode(obj, 'EDIT'):
    bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action='SELECT')
    bpy.ops.mesh.fill_grid(use_interp_simple=True)
